title: prefill/decode: chunked + speculative prefill and stage overlap for throughput
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce tail latency and increase steady-state throughput for workloads with long prefill contexts and mixed prefill/decode traffic. Prefill-heavy requests currently monopolize KV/cache memory and GPU scheduling slots which increases queueing for low-latency decode requests. This PR implements three complementary optimizations: chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage overlap (pipeline prefill+decode). Approach: 1) Chunked prefill: split long prefill requests into configurable chunks that materialize KV cache incrementally. This limits transient memory pressure and allows earlier decode work to start for other micro-batches. 2) Speculative prefill: for common prefix patterns and monotonic next-token heuristics we launch the next prefill chunk in a best-effort background worker while decode is still running on the previous chunk; speculation is bounded by a budget and can be disabled per-customer. 3) Stage overlap (pipeline): runtime scheduler was extended to allow prefill and decode stages to run concurrently across different micro-batches. The runtime now tracks stage dependencies and enforces resource caps to ensure decode-critical work is prioritized while background prefill proceeds without blocking latency SLOs. Kernel and KV changes: fused attention kernels updated to support partial KV writes and incremental KV layout so chunked inserts avoid memcpy storms. KV cache implemented a reader/priority-writer lock and checkpointing so speculative/partial writes can be rolled back if mis-speculated. Scheduling: new scheduler hooks with priority classes (decode-critical, background-prefill, low) and a per-GPU token quota for speculative workers. Continuous batching: batch splitter updated to form decode micro-batches independent of prefill chunk boundaries so decodes can keep GPUs busy. Backwards-compatible flags: new config flags runtime.prefill.chunk_size, runtime.prefill.speculative_budget, runtime.prefill.stage_overlap_enabled. Default behavior preserves previous semantics (chunking disabled) unless runtime config toggles optimizations. Testing and validation: unit tests for KV partial writes, concurrency stress tests for speculative rollback, integration perf test harness added under tests/perf/test_prefill_overlap.py. Benchmarks and canary: local perf-canary harness and cluster canary ran across A10G and A100 nodes. Results show 12-22% P95 latency reduction for medium-length contexts (2k-4k tokens) and up to 30% throughput increase under mixed prefill/decode workloads on 7B and 13B models. Rollout plan: gated feature behind runtime flag and staged rollout to Dedicated customers with opt-in via console. Monitoring: new metrics added (prefill.chunk_count, prefill.speculative_attempts, prefill.speculative_rollbacks, prefill.stage_overlap_active) and tracing hooks for pipeline stages. Limitations: speculative prefill improves common-case patterns but may increase wasted compute if mis-speculated; budgets prevent runaway cost. This PR includes documentation updates and a changelog entry. See linked linear tickets for follow-ups such as adaptive chunk sizing and ML-driven speculation heuristics.
